ai.1.note: Assistant tab: EN/FR rule-based commands (move stops with customer notice, briefing, late stops, forecast, reports). Changes ask for confirmation. An AI key adds a model fallback whose answer is checked the same way; not tested against the real service.

ai.10.note: Jobs per day and drivers needed for the next week from history, with a range and a shortfall warning.

ai.11.note: Address tidy (street types, capitals, postal code spacing, province codes, unit order) then look-up in saved places and the map provider.

ai.12.note: Reading photos needs an AI key (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY); without it the endpoint answers 503 and the UI says so. Not tested against the real service.

ai.2.note: Describe a report in words (template, period, grouping) and save it to Reports. Rule-based; the model fallback needs an AI key and is untested against the real service.

ai.3.note: Daily briefing on the Assistant page, most urgent first, with links.

ai.4.note: Explains lateness from late start, long or failed stops, help requests, weather, idling and slower driving. No live traffic feed, so traffic is never named as a cause.

ai.5.note: Late-risk list from remaining time against windows, with a chance and a level. A transparent calculation, not a trained model.

ai.6.note: Vehicle health score from service history, defects, fuel use, repairs, downtime, incidents and age. A transparent score, not a trained model.

ai.7.note: Auto-assign and suggestions score skills, distance, load, on-time record, customer rating and past visits to the customer.

ai.8.note: Learned stop time per customer (after 3 visits), shown next to the planned time with a one-click apply.

ai.9.note: Planner learns speed by hour of day from your trips; per-driver speed is used too. Shown on the Learned tab.

alerts.1.note: Alert rules for late risk, off route, long idle, speeding and geofence entry or exit, plus offline vehicles, harsh driving, expiring documents, due maintenance, cost spikes and any number crossing a limit.

alerts.10.note: Forecast of next week stops, cost and drive hours with what is already booked.

alerts.11.note: The ask box understands common questions such as "which driver had the most delays last month?" with a rule-based reader and answers with a number or chart. Free-form questions come with the AI helper in Phase 5.

alerts.2.note: Rule builder with plain-words summary and a "test the rule" button.

alerts.3.note: In-app inbox, Slack, Teams and webhooks are built and tested against a stand-in server. Email and SMS need an email key or Twilio account on the server and were not tried live. Browser or phone push is not built.

alerts.4.note: Quiet hours (critical alerts still go out) and grouping so the same problem is not repeated.

alerts.5.note: Morning summary at 7:00 of what was held back.

alerts.6.note: Cost anomaly rule and insight cards use a robust statistic against the last month.

alerts.7.note: Insight cards in plain English or French (for example: a route late on most recent days).

alerts.8.note: Goals with targets and progress bars for a day, week or month.

alerts.9.note: Benchmarks compare drivers, vehicles, depots and routes against the middle of the group.

auto.1.note: No-code workflows: pick a trigger, match rules (all/any) and actions; templates gallery and a Try it test run. Automation page.

auto.10.note: HMAC-signed webhooks on any event, delivery log, retries with back-off (1, 5, 30, 120, 720 minutes), ping, secret rotation.

auto.2.note: Built-in minutes-away trigger plus a customer message in the customer's language; also available as a workflow template.

auto.3.note: Routes are replanned when a stop is cancelled or removed. Live traffic and crash detection need a traffic feed and are not built.

auto.4.note: Invoice INV-YYYY-NNNN is created when a job is marked done (workflow action and default setting); PDF download in the portal.

auto.5.note: Public booking form creates orders and a workflow can assign them. Email, store and form connectors need outside accounts.

auto.6.note: Needs-break alert rule (hours without a break) feeds the event feed, workflows and the dispatcher inbox.

auto.7.note: Unaccepted-job escalation as a workflow trigger with a minutes setting (default 15); notifies the manager.

auto.8.note: Recurring route templates, maintenance plans and scheduled reports.

auto.9.note: Approvals queue for overtime, expenses over the limit and workflow approvals; decide with a note; sidebar count.

builder.1.note: Report builder: pick data, columns, filters, grouping and sorting.

builder.10.note: PDF reports carry the company logo, name and colour from settings.

builder.11.note: Public share links with an expiry date, a visible list and one-click turn-off.

builder.12.note: Embed a shared report in another page with an iframe (add ?embed=1).

builder.13.note: A shared link can be limited to one driver, vehicle or depot. Restricting what each signed-in person sees by depot or team is not built.

builder.14.note: Every save keeps a version; restore any earlier one.

builder.2.note: Save reports, keep versions, share with the team, and start from 16 templates.

builder.3.note: Click a chart mark or a grouped row to drill into the rows behind it (scorecards open their stops). It stops at the route; it does not yet jump to a single trip replay.

builder.5.note: Calculated fields with a safe formula box (for example cost / stops).

builder.6.note: Charts: line, bar, stacked, pie, heat map, funnel, scatter and map, each with a table view.

builder.7.note: Map reports: a heat map of stops or driving events.

builder.8.note: Daily, weekly and monthly schedules to Slack, Teams, webhooks, email or SMS are built and tested against a stand-in server. Email and SMS need a mail-service key or a Twilio account set up on the server, and none of it was tried against the real services.

builder.9.note: PDF, Excel and CSV exports work. For Google Sheets, a shared report CSV link can be pulled in with the IMPORTDATA formula; there is no direct Google connection.

cust.1.note: Branded live tracking page /j/<token> with map, ETA and company colours.

cust.10.note: Rating and comment after each delivery; shown to managers.

cust.11.note: Customer portal with orders, invoices (PDF) and support chat.

cust.12.note: Public booking page with quote and spam protection.

cust.13.note: Public status page with your own notices.

cust.14.note: Per-customer notification preferences on the tracking link.

cust.15.note: Message templates in EN/FR with company logo and colours; wording editor with preview.

cust.16.note: Proof photos shown as a gallery on the job page.

cust.17.note: Help centre FAQ page and support chat in the portal and job page.

cust.18.note: Loyalty and referral features chosen not to build for now.

cust.19.note: Return and pickup requests from the tracking link.

cust.2.note: Customer picks a delivery slot when rescheduling or booking.

cust.20.note: All public pages in English and French.

cust.3.note: In-product messages and templates work; email and SMS send through your provider keys, WhatsApp is not built. Needs outside accounts.

cust.4.note: Driver-is-N-stops-away notice on the tracking page and as a trigger.

cust.5.note: Reschedule and cancel from the tracking link, with the rules you set.

cust.6.note: Customers leave delivery instructions (gate code, leave at door); shown on the driver's stop.

cust.7.note: Driver name, photo and vehicle on the tracking page.

cust.8.note: Chat with dispatch is built. A masked phone number needs a telephony account.

cust.9.note: Proof of delivery link with photo and signature on the job page.

dash.1.note: Executive template: cost, on-time rate, utilization, customer score, trends, goals, insights and forecast. Cost uses the per-km and per-hour rates in settings.

dash.10.note: TV wall mode: full screen, big numbers, refreshes every minute, Esc to leave.

dash.11.note: One set of filters (dates, depot, driver, vehicle) for every widget. There is no separate "region" or "team" field yet, so depots stand in for them.

dash.12.note: Compare with the previous period or the same dates last year; every key number shows the change.

dash.2.note: Operations template: live jobs, late stops, idling vehicles (refreshes every 30 seconds).

dash.3.note: Driver template, and a "My numbers" sheet in the driver app: score, stops, on-time rate, distance, safety events and an estimated pay.

dash.4.note: A customer-service template (deliveries, delays, failed reasons, ratings by customer) for your staff. A dashboard that customers sign in to comes with the customer portal in Phase 4.

dash.5.note: Finance template: cost per route, stop, kilometre, hour and vehicle.

dash.6.note: Safety template: speeding, harsh braking and acceleration found in GPS tracks, incidents, driver score.

dash.7.note: Sustainability template: fuel, CO2, fuel economy, idle share and savings from applied route optimization (assumes 30 L per 100 km).

dash.8.note: Customize: add, remove, resize and drag widgets (or use the up and down buttons), then save as your own dashboard and share it with the team.

dash.9.note: Seven templates by role; the page opens on the one that fits your role.

dispatch.1.note: Dispatch board: unassigned jobs and one lane per driver; drag a job onto a lane or use the menu.

dispatch.10.note: Select stops to split onto a new route, or merge another route in.

dispatch.2.note: Auto-assign suggests the best driver by skills, capacity, shift and distance, then applies on one click.

dispatch.3.note: Pickup, delivery, service call and inspection jobs.

dispatch.4.note: Low to urgent priority; the rush button inserts an urgent job and says what it delays.

dispatch.5.note: Reassign from the board or the job panel; the driver's route updates and the change is logged.

dispatch.6.note: Unassigned, assigned, started, arrived, done, failed; stop changes update the job automatically.

dispatch.7.note: Photo and signature (earlier milestone) plus package-code scans. Camera scanning needs a browser with BarcodeDetector (Chrome on Android); typing the code works everywhere. Not tried on a real phone.

dispatch.8.note: Notes, tags and file attachments on jobs.

dispatch.9.note: Cancel and reschedule ask for a reason code; history is kept.

driver.1.note: Installable web app (manifest and service worker). Native iOS and Android store apps are not built.

driver.11.note: Chat with the dispatcher in the driver app, offline-safe through the outbox; dispatcher inbox replies.

driver.12.note: Quick replies (late, arrived, need help ...) in EN/FR with one tap.

driver.13.note: In-app alerts use the browser Notification API when the app is open. Background push needs a push provider account.

driver.14.note: Shift clock: start, end, breaks, overtime flags; timesheets page for managers with approval.

driver.15.note: Break and lunch timer with a reminder when a break is due.

driver.17.note: Expense sheet with receipt photo; auto-approved under the limit, otherwise sent for approval; reimburse in Expenses.

driver.18.note: Tips sheet and trip/earnings summary in the driver app.

driver.19.note: Battery-saver mode lowers update rate and turns animations off; savings not measured on devices.

driver.2.note: Offline outbox and service worker; actions sync when signal returns.

driver.20.note: Driver app in English and French.

driver.21.note: Biometric sign-in needs the native app or passkeys on real hardware; not built in the web app.

driver.22.note: Apple Watch, CarPlay and Android Auto need native apps and platform approval; not built.

driver.23.note: Mark a stop failed with a reason and photo.

driver.24.note: Help request (flat tire, wrong address, customer not home) with notes; dispatcher acknowledges or resolves in Inbox.

driver.25.note: Training items and tips managed in Settings and shown in the driver app.

driver.4.note: One-tap open in Google Maps, Waze or Apple Maps. No built-in turn-by-turn.

driver.5.note: Voice commands (EN/FR) with a confirm step and voice notes use browser speech and recording support; not verified on real phones.

driver.7.note: Driving mode (big buttons, locked controls) while moving; browsers cannot truly lock the phone screen. Not verified on devices.

driver.8.note: Barcode and QR scanner (uses the browser's detector where available).

driver.9.note: Photo capture with timestamp and location on proofs.

ds.1.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.2.note: Dashboard cards come in 1 to 4 column sizes on a grid (Dashboards page).

ds.3.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.4.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.5.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.6.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.7.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.8.note: Tokens, one accent plus grays, success/warning/danger/info, 8-point grid, Inter + Manrope, type scale, Lucide icons, components (Button, Input, Table, Modal, Tabs, Chip, KPI, Toast, Skeleton).

ds.9.note: A living style guide page at /styleguide. Storybook itself was not added.

fleet.1.note: Vehicle records with photo, plate, VIN, capacity, fuel type, EV range and more.

fleet.10.note: Trip log from vehicle movement with business or personal tags and CSV export.

fleet.2.note: Driver profiles: licence, emergency contact, shift limits, skills, training; documents attach to drivers too.

fleet.3.note: Document and licence expiry reminders on the Maintenance page. Emailing them out comes with Phase 4 alerts.

fleet.4.note: Maintenance plans by days or kilometres, due and overdue state, mark-done history.

fleet.5.note: Fuel logs, fuel economy per vehicle and CSV import of fuel-card statements. Live feeds from card companies need their accounts.

fleet.6.note: Trailers and equipment with status and assignment.

fleet.7.note: Check-out and check-in checklist in the driver app; a failed item records a defect and shows in reminders.

fleet.8.note: Incident reports from the driver app with location and photos, tracked from open to closed on the office side.

fleet.9.note: Depot records with parking spots; live occupancy is calculated by the API but not shown in the screens yet.

kpi.1.note: On-time delivery rate, from stop arrival times against time windows.

kpi.10.note: Customer satisfaction (1 to 5) and NPS from ratings on the tracking page or entered by the office.

kpi.13.note: Route adherence is measured against straight lines between stops (within 600 m), so it is a rough guide. A road-based check needs the routing service switched on.

kpi.14.note: Vehicle downtime hours and repair cost from maintenance logs.

kpi.15.note: Driver overtime hours (after the daily hours set in settings).

kpi.3.note: Average delay and worst delay in minutes.

kpi.4.note: Cost per stop, per kilometre and per hour. These are estimates from the rates in settings; fuel and repair costs are shown as their own numbers.

kpi.5.note: Utilization (engine hours against a shift) and load fill (weight against vehicle capacity).

kpi.6.note: Idle time, idle share and engine-on time from GPS.

kpi.7.note: Planned versus actual distance and time per route.

kpi.9.note: Fuel economy (L per 100 km) per vehicle from fuel logs, and per driver where the fill-up names the driver.

live.10.note: Expiring, revocable share links with a public tracking page. It shows no driver name or plate and is rate-limited.

live.2.note: Trail on the map and day-by-day replay (milestone 3).

live.3.note: Draw circle or polygon zones on a map; enter and exit events are recorded as vehicles move. Sending them out as alerts comes with Phase 4 alerts.

live.4.note: ETAs refresh as vehicles move. They react to real traffic only once a live traffic source is connected.

live.5.note: Moving, idle, stopped and offline colours.

live.7.note: Heat layers for stops, late deliveries and speeding on the live map.

live.8.note: Street and satellite switch, plus a Street View link.

live.9.note: Weather at a vehicle and at each stop's arrival time, from Open-Meteo. Needs internet access to that service; tested only against a stub.

motion.1.note: Skeleton loaders on every list and table.

motion.10.note: Account menu has Follow device / Reduce motion / Full motion; it also respects the device setting.

motion.2.note: Short fade and slide transitions on dialogs, toasts and panels. No full page transitions.

motion.3.note: Planned with the route map in Phase 2.

motion.4.note: Vehicle markers glide to each new fix (lib/glide.ts).

motion.6.note: Buttons press, switches slide, menus fade.

motion.8.note: Planned with the driver app in Phase 4.

motion.9.note: Planned with the dispatch board in Phase 2.

nav.1.note: Collapsible side menu; becomes a drawer on phones.

nav.10.note: Home dashboard with drag-and-drop widgets arrives with dashboards in Phase 3.

nav.3.note: Searches vehicles, drivers, routes and stops. Customers join when customer records are added.

nav.5.note: History and route pages: list on the left, map on the right.

nav.6.note: Drag the divider (or use the arrow keys); the width is remembered.

nav.7.note: Pin any page; pins show in the menu and in the palette.

nav.8.note: ? opens the cheat sheet; g then l/r/p jumps; T switches theme; [ collapses the menu.

nav.9.note: Tables save named views (sort, filters, columns, grouping). Custom tabs are not built.

opt.1.note: Multi-depot preview and apply: each job goes to the nearest depot and its drivers.

opt.10.note: Driver wishes (most stops, days off, customers to avoid) and skills are respected in auto-assign. Customers to avoid affect suggestions only.

opt.2.note: Suggested compact areas (clustering), saved areas with a driver each; the planner keeps drivers in their areas.

opt.3.note: Workload spread and fairness check with suggested stop moves that can be applied.

opt.4.note: Compare as-planned, fastest and shortest order with fuel, wages, wear and tolls; apply the cheapest order.

opt.5.note: Lowest-CO2 option flagged, plus CO2 if another vehicle drove the route.

opt.6.note: Open pick-ups near the road back to the depot, within spare capacity.

opt.8.note: Pickup before delivery with the same driver; the planner enforces it and a fix button repairs broken pairs.

opt.9.note: What-if: add or remove vehicles, change shift length, capacity or depot and compare against today's plan.

polish.1.note: Empty states say what to do next.

polish.10.note: Five-step product tour and a getting-started checklist for owners and admins.

polish.11.note: Tooltips and a What's new panel.

polish.2.note: Plain-language error states with a retry button and a separate "no access" state.

polish.3.note: Undo for deleting a stop (toast with Undo). Other deletes and edits get it as their screens are built.

polish.4.note: Double-click a cell to edit (people names).

polish.5.note: Sort, filter, group, pin, hide and resize columns, CSV export, saved views.

polish.6.note: Sticky headers; lists over 150 rows are windowed.

polish.8.note: Keyboard use, labels and focus are in place; axe found no contrast problems in the three themes. Not tested with a real screen reader.

polish.9.note: English and French complete. Punjabi and Arabic cover sign-in, navigation and the driver app; Arabic mirrors the layout. Both were drafted without a native reviewer.

report.10.note: Geofence visits template with time spent in each zone.

report.12.note: Compliance report lists shift hours, failed inspections and expiring documents. Legal hours-of-service rules are not built.

report.13.note: A billing template with a price-per-stop formula you can change. Invoice numbers, tax and customer contracts are not built.

report.14.note: Audit log page with filters and CSV export.

report.15.note: One-page executive summary as a branded PDF (button on the Dashboards page).

report.7.note: Exceptions template: late, failed and skipped stops.

report.8.note: A mileage template (km and engine hours per vehicle). The business and personal split lives in the Trip log, not yet in this report.

report.9.note: Fuel and emissions template (CO2 from fuel type).

route.1.note: Drag stops to reorder on the route page (keyboard works too). apps/web/src/app/(app)/routes/[id].

route.10.note: Save any route as a template; create routes from templates.

route.11.note: Daily, weekly and custom repeats; the scheduler creates each day's routes once (no duplicates).

route.12.note: CSV import of jobs, with errors listed by row. Excel files are not read directly: save as CSV first.

route.13.note: Address search with saved places and 'did you mean' fixes. Live address lookup needs a geocoding service (Nominatim or similar); tested only against a stub.

route.14.note: Current order vs optimized order shown side by side with cost, time and late stops.

route.15.note: Drop a pin and see where an extra stop fits and what becomes late, before saving.

route.2.note: Optimizer for shortest time or distance (cheapest insertion + 2-opt/or-opt), unit-tested. Uses real road times when a routing engine is set (ROUTING_URL); otherwise straight-line estimates, and the screen says so.

route.3.note: Time windows per stop, treated as hard limits by the optimizer and flagged when late.

route.4.note: Weight, volume and item limits per vehicle; over-capacity is flagged on the board and respected by auto-assign.

route.5.note: Max shift length and mandatory breaks per driver; the optimizer inserts breaks.

route.6.note: Predicted ETAs use hourly speed patterns learned from your own vehicles' positions. Live traffic needs an outside traffic data source.

route.7.note: Avoid tolls, highways, ferries and unpaved roads are sent to the routing engine (OSRM or Valhalla). Enforcing them needs a routing engine; not run in the sandbox.

route.8.note: Height, weight and hazmat limits are sent to Valhalla's truck profile. Needs a Valhalla server; tested only against a stub.

route.9.note: Planner tracks battery range and adds charging stops. Real charger locations need an outside data source, so charge points are entered by you.

safety.1.note: Score from speeding, hard braking, hard acceleration and cornering per 100 km. Phone-use detection needs a native app and is not built.

safety.2.note: Driver app shows up to 3 tips after trips, based on the driver's own numbers.

safety.3.note: Opt-in ranking, names hidden by default, with positive badges only.

safety.4.note: Bonus rules per week or month; Calculate creates each bonus once; marking paid stays manual.

safety.5.note: Warns after the set hours without a break; shown to the driver and on the Live tab; raises an alert rule.

safety.6.note: SOS button in the driver app; works offline (queued) and appears in the inbox with position.

safety.7.note: Phone motion and GPS crash check asks the driver first, then tells dispatch. Not tested in a real crash or on real devices.

safety.8.note: Stores links to dash-cam clips beside events; the video itself is never stored or fetched.

safety.9.note: Lone-worker check-ins with a schedule; a missed check-in raises an alert.

security.2.note: Append-only audit log of every change with who, what, when and IP; the app role cannot edit or delete it.

style.1.note: Tokens and components follow a clean, minimal look (apps/web/src/app/tokens.css).

style.2.note: Bento dashboard cards arrive with the dashboards in Phase 3.

style.3.note: Floating map panel uses a light blur; switched off in high-contrast mode.

style.4.note: Dark theme and a dark basemap work. Glowing route lines are not done.

style.5.note: The Playbook says pick one direction and stay with it; soft shadows hurt readability.

style.6.note: Live map fills the page with panels floating on top.

teams.1.note: Owner, admin, dispatcher, manager, driver, customer and read-only. Customer and driver land in their own apps (the customer portal arrives in Phase 4).

teams.2.note: Custom roles with fine-grained permissions (Settings > People & roles).

teams.4.note: Every table is tenant-isolated with Row-Level Security (since Milestone 1); tests prove it.

theme.1.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.2.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.3.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.4.note: Light, dark, follow-the-device and high-contrast themes; picked from the account menu or with the T key.

theme.5.note: Each company sets a brand color and logo in Settings. The color is adjusted so text stays readable (tests in lib/color.test.ts).

theme.6.note: Okabe-Ito palette in --chart-1 to --chart-8, used by every chart.

theme.7.note: The palette exists; route lines on maps adopt it in Phase 2.
